content: Heads-up for t9/t8: Codec/Json.lean is complete and lake build is green. Import it with `import Codec.Json` (Codec.lean re-exports). Types you may need live in namespace Codec: ClientMessage (19 ctors), MirrorMessage (20), ValidateResult, TraceGenResult, JobKind/JobPhase/JobOutcome, PathSeg/DiffKind/DiffHint (DiffHint is a structure with kind/path/actual?/expected? — NOT in Core), ApalacheConfig/SpecConfig/TraceConfig. Encoders: Codec.encodeClient/encodeMirror (and encodeValue for ITF). Decoders: decodeClient/decodeMirror/decodeValue (total, Except DecodeError). §6.6 value round-trip theorem available as Codec.decodeValue_encValue for reuse.

Captain directive (from the user) for t9: the session machine and the §6.3 TlaStep encoding MUST be faithful to the authoritative spec at /home/nzsn/Repos/ModelMirros/specs/MirrorProtocol.tla (578 lines, ModelMirros@3496251 — the same pin the fixtures use; record this pin in a module doc comment). I have read the full spec; subtleties your encoding must capture exactly: (1) mirror state is phase × mirror_flow ('none'|'traces'|'session'|'validate') — flow is part of the state, not derivable; (2) MirrorRecvRegisterTraces is a FAST PATH: idle→ready emitting SPEC_VALIDATED immediately, no validating phase (unlike Register/RegisterExplore/RegisterExploreSession/RegisterValidate which go idle→validating); (3) MirrorSendSpecValidatedValid BRANCHES on flow: traces→ready, validate→done; (4) MirrorRecvReportOk queues STEP_OK and NEXT_STEP is sent by a separate action (MirrorSendNextStep) requiring both queues empty — model Core.step's output list accordingly; (5) the three Report outcomes (Ok/AllDone/Mismatch) are distinct transitions; (6) invariants to state mirror-side: PhaseOk (mirror_phase ∈ 7 phases) and the mirror obligations of ClientNeverStuck; (7) async-job and explorer-session extensions are NOT in the TLA+ spec — state them as explicit extensions of TlaStep per doc §6.3, clearly separated from the faithful core. 19 message tags REGISTER..EXPLORE_DONE (0..18). If any Core.step behavior cannot be mapped to a TlaStep transition, STOP and report to me before deviating.

Understood, thanks — Codec → Core layering with tag-abstract messages at the protocol layer makes sense, and a driver-boundary bridge (Codec.ClientMessage → Core.ClientMessage + tag fidelity) fits naturally as a small follow-up if it's ever wanted. For the record on what Codec.Json now exposes for such a bridge: decodeClient_encodeClient / decodeMirror_encodeMirror (message round-trips, all 39 ctors, exact on scalar-only ctors), decodeValue_encValue + decValueF_encValue (value-level, fuel-parameterized), and the wireOk/valBounded/ClientOk/MirrorOk side conditions — tag extraction itself is just jStr (encodeM m) "proto_step" via getObjVal?_mkObj. Happy to take that bridge task if the captain creates it; otherwise idle.

Thanks — very useful. Noted for a potential bridge task: target Core.ClientMessage (16 ctors, reportState w/ matches/lastStep Bools) / Core.MirrorMessage (with never-emitted protocolError), obligation = tag-name/position fidelity only (AllowedOutputs exactness + no_unsolicited_output cover reachability). On the Codec side the tag map is mechanical: jStr (encodeClient m) "proto_step" via getObjVal?_mkObj; reportState carries ValueMap in Codec (not the Bools), so the bridge will need to source matches/lastStep elsewhere at the driver boundary — exactly the payload-at-driver split you described. I'm idle too.

Both already fixed and t10 is completed (full build + lake test green on my side, just re-verified): (1) Shell.lean imports moved before the module docstring; (2) confirmed IO.getArgs is gone in the 4.33 toolchain core (grepped Init/System — no such constant) — Main.lean now reads argv from /proc/self/cmdline (POSIX-only, documented, same platform caveat as Phase 6 signals). Re tag mapping: Shell.Mirror.Session does have a hand-rolled Codec.ClientMessage → Core tag mapping (dispatch + the reportState matches/lastStep bits computed via Core.diffState); it's small and isolated inside Shell/Mirror/Session.lean, so swapping in codec-engineer's proven t22 bridge when it lands will be a local change. Phase 3 exit criterion is verified: the Haskell 'mbt over stdio' integration suite passes against .lake/build/bin/mirror.

Thanks — very useful. Confirmed on my side too: t12 (Phase 4 job store) is complete and green; full lake build is now 46 jobs (added jobstore_spec exe + Shell.Jobs.Store/Shell.Transport.Mock modules) and lake test runs all four gates green. Noted for the t22 swap: per-phase exact AllowedOutputs, protocolError never emitted by Core.step, and t20's wire-ordered hints — the Session hand-rolled mapping in Shell/Mirror/Session.lean is isolated to dispatch/sendMirror + the async dispatch in runAsync, so replacing it with the Codec bridge should be a contained diff on my side. One parity caveat codec-engineer should keep in mind when the bridge lands: Shell.Mirror.Session still carries a normNums workaround (normalizing bare integral JSON numbers to {"#bigint": ...} before Codec.decodeValue) for the Haskell FromJSON bare-number gap I reported earlier — if t22 touches decodeValue, that workaround either gets absorbed there or should be dropped deliberately.

All already handled, thanks for the forward: (1) t22 bridge landed (Codec/Bridge.lean — protoClientTag/protoMirrorTag/concreteMirror + 40 tag-fidelity theorems + allowed_outputs_have_concrete); (2) the bare-number gap is fixed IN Codec.decodeValue itself (t23, in flight): decValueF accepts any value-integral bare number as VInt exactly per Haskell FromJSON (2.0→2, 3e2→300, 0.5 rejected), so normNums is now redundant — shell-engineer has been asked to drop it and re-run the stdio suite before I close t23. Good to know diffState hint wire order is exact per t20 — no codec-side change needed for that.
